text:
For twenty minutes, Florida did almost everything right and trailed 3-1 anyway. The Panthers out-chanced Boston 2.03 to 1.14 in expected goals (the quality of chances) in the first period, and Brady Tkachuk had the best look of the game, a 23% chance that Jeremy Swayman turned away. At the other end, Elias Lindholm scored at 4:50 on a 4% wrist shot, the least likely goal of the afternoon, and Michael Eyssimont poked one in 81 seconds later.

That was the game, and our win-probability numbers say so: Lindholm's goal moved Boston from 53% to 67%, Eyssimont's to 80%. Morgan Geekie added a power-play slap shot at 15:59, set up by David Pastrnak and Pavel Zacha, before Carter Verhaeghe answered on a Florida power play with both Tkachuks assisting. JJ Peterka put it away 58 seconds into the third, again off Pastrnak and Zacha.

Swayman was the difference. He stopped 40 of 41 shots, 2.8 goals more than those shots deserved, and added a third of a win by our count, more than anyone on the ice. Florida actually deserved to win 54% of the time on these chances, and took 62 shot attempts to Boston's 53. Jacob Markstrom allowed four on 36 shots, roughly what the shots were worth, but his last five starts have been rough (.874).

Boston is 13-4-1 and has won four straight, and the Pastrnak and Zacha partnership that Daily Faceoff just called one of the league's elite duos keeps producing. The caution is the same as it's been all season: the Bruins are winning more than their chances suggest, with goaltending saving them goals. Florida, playing the second day of a back-to-back after losing in Washington, has dropped two in a row and sits at 9-7-2. With Anton Lundell barely back from injury, the Panthers are getting the chances and not the goals. That usually turns. It didn't on Sunday.
headline: Swayman makes 40 saves and the Bruins win four straight
